title: Polyglot prefetch + telemetry-aware iterator for embeddings and rerank
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a polyglot (Python/TypeScript/Go) iterator + helper library that combines pagination, batching, prefetch, and telemetry hooks for Embeddings and Rerank endpoints. The goal is to provide a single ergonomic primitive across SDKs that simplifies common patterns: paginated source reads, efficient batching to the API, resumable streaming, and automatic retry/backoff with observable metrics for cost/latency breakdowns.
background: Customers implement similar iterator/prefetch patterns in product code to stream large document sets into embeddings and rerank endpoints. Existing SDK helpers are fragmented across languages and focus on either batching or pagination but not telemetry-driven adaptation. This causes duplication, subtle bugs around retries and checkpoints, and poor visibility into token/cost distribution when using our APIs at scale.
goals: Ship a language-consistent iterator helper in Python, TypeScript, and Go that supports pagination, windowed batching, and prefetching
Add first-class telemetry hooks (latency, tokens per batch, retry counts, items processed) that integrate with Redwood Console and local dev logs
Provide safe defaults for retries/backoff and a simple config surface for advanced users
Include examples and cookbook recipes for common workflows (embeddings indexing, batched rerank over N candidates, resumable flows)
non_goals: Providing heavy-weight opinionated orchestration (this is a lightweight SDK helper)
success_metrics: Reduce copy-paste iterator code in customer and internal examples by 80% across sample apps
Improve average per-batch latency observability in Console for instrumented customers
Decrease customer-reported integration bugs for retries/pagination by 60% within two quarters
acceptance_criteria: Python, TypeScript, and Go packages publish a v0.1 helper with identical API shape (method names and config options)
Unit tests cover retry edge cases, resume-after-failure, and correct batching behavior
Integration example notebooks/demos for embeddings indexing and rerank batching added to the SDK examples repo
Telemetry events emitted are documented and visible in a staging Console org (latency_ms, tokens_sent, retries, batch_size)
design_summary: Core primitive: PrefetchIterator<T> wraps a paginated source (sync/async) and exposes an async iterator that yields batches of items. Key features: adaptive prefetch window, batch transformer that maps items -> API requests (embeddings vs rerank), pluggable retry/backoff policy, resume token checkpointing callback, and telemetry hooks fired per-batch and per-retry. API shape is intentionally small: constructor(config), mapToBatches(batchFn), for await yield batches, checkpoint(token) optional. Provide a sync shim for Go and ergonomic async/await for Python/TS. Defaults favor low-latency (small batches) for interactive flows and provide a 'throughput' preset for bulk indexing.
python_notes:
- Provide AsyncPrefetchIterator and SyncPrefetchIterator wrappers.
- Retry model: decorated with hikari-style exponential backoff + jitter; default retryable errors: 5xx, 429, transient network errors.
- Expose `telemetry_client` arg that accepts a function or object with `emit(event_name, tags, value)` to integrate with Console or local logger.
- Example snippet included in examples/python/indexer.py
typescript_notes:
- Expose `PrefetchIterator<T>` compatible with for-await-of.
- Provide built-in browser-safe fallbacks for backoff timers to avoid blocking main thread.
- Default bundling for bundlers: keep size small, tree-shakable export of helpers only.
- Example in examples/ts/embedding-indexer.ts
go_notes:
- Provide synchronous iterator with channels and context.Context cancellation.
- Backoff implementation uses math/rand jitter and integrates with the runtime's tracing/telemetry via a simple interface `TelemetrySink` (Emit(name, tags, value)).
- Because Go doesn't have native async/await, we provide a `StartPrefetch(ctx)` method that spawns prefetch goroutines and returns a channel of batches.
telemetry_schema: Events emitted: 'batch_sent' (tags: sdk_lang, endpoint, batch_size, tokens_estimated; value: latency_ms), 'batch_retry' (tags: sdk_lang, endpoint, attempt, error_code), 'checkpoint' (tags: sdk_lang, endpoint, items_processed), 'prefetch_window' (tags: sdk_lang, endpoint; value: current_window) - documented and versioned. Use semantic keys so Console can parse out token/cost metrics.
api_examples: Python async: iterator = AsyncPrefetchIterator(source=pagination_fn, batch_size=32, prefetch=2, retry_policy='default'); async for batch in iterator.map_to_api(request_builder): await client.embeddings.create(batch)
TypeScript: const it = new PrefetchIterator(paginate, {batchSize: 16, prefetch: 3}); for await (const batch of it.map(mapToDocEmbeddings)) { await api.embeddings.create({input: batch}) }
Go: it := NewPrefetchIterator(ctx, paginateFn, PrefetchOptions{BatchSize:20, Prefetch:4}); for batch := range it.StartPrefetch(ctx) { resp, err := client.Embeddings.Create(ctx, batch) }
retry_backoff_defaults: Exponential backoff with base=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max_backoff=10s, max_attempts=5. Jitter=full. Idempotency: the helper makes best-effort to avoid duplicate processing by checkpoint callbacks; users can opt-in to at-least-once behavior for throughput work.
migration_notes:
- Mark previous helpers deprecated in next minor release with guidance mapping old helper calls to new PrefetchIterator usage.
- Provide codemods/snippets in SDK changelog and migration doc.
- Add feature flag to enable telemetry emission for customers that need approval.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Land library changes in internal feature branch, unit tests + linting
Week 2: Publish v0.1 in all three SDKs behind feature flag; add examples to examples/ repo
Week 3: Enable telemetry emission in staging org and validate Console parses events
Week 4: Iterate on perf knobs and update docs; announce in SDK changelog and deprecation notice for old helpers
test_plan: Unit tests for batch partitioning, prefetch window adjustment, and retry behavior (simulate transient failures)
Integration test against staging API to assert telemetry events appear and tokens_sent approximations are reasonable
Fuzz tests for pagination edge cases (empty pages, varying page sizes), cancellation behavior in Go and Python
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Telemetry volume could be high for bulk jobs - Mitigation: make telemetry opt-in by default and provide sampling config
Risk: Behavioral mismatch across SDKs - Mitigation: maintain single spec file for API surface and run cross-language conformance tests
Risk: Increased latency from over-aggressive prefetch - Mitigation: conservative defaults and 'throughput' preset for bulk users
